Does it make a difference if you season while cooking or wait until the very end to season?
I was always taught that salt should be one of the last seasonings (and used toward the end of the cooking) because it draws out the moisture.
Unless the salt is dissolved in a marinade, yeah.
Veggies turn out awesome if seasoned while they cook. I usually season while cooking, for anything that will take a long time.(low and slow)

I typically do most/base seasoning before cooking. Take for example brining meat, that's always done before cooking. Same with making jerky.

On the other hand, when I make stir-fry, it's usually later on during the process.

Making spaghetti sauce, most is done on the fly during the cooking.

It depends. For meats, season first, and that includes salt. Oil the meat rather than the pan, season, and let it rest. Salt will draw out moisture from the meat, dissolve, then soak back in, seasoning the interior. The process is called koshering, and course salts are best for it. Bring red meat to temp, fish and poultry need to rest in the fridge.

Some herbs and spices also have compounds that are volatile in fats, so seasoning while cooking will bring out or deepen flavors. Cumin, for example. I also like to toast fennel.

I essentially do things in stages. The stir fry I made a few days ago went like: Salt, pepper and oil the chicken, toss that in. Once it had some color on it, soy sauce and garlic, and let that reduce. Veggies in, let those cook for a few minutes, then some sesame seed, and a few minutes more.

Theres really no one answer to be honest. With poached eggs, I salt the water, with scrambled I season afterwards, and with omelets I mix the seasonings in.
